tldr: US rebounded hard Monday (Nasdaq +1.11%, VIX -7.75% to 18.44) after Goldman upgraded CoreWeave, but Oracle and SpaceX CDS spreads both hit FRESH records -- AI-credit stress has narrowed, not resolved, directly relevant to the GDX/SILJ/SLVP sleeve's AI-adjacent read-throughs.

Gold/silver pulled back modestly (gold -0.61%, silver +0.09%) on profit-taking as risk appetite improved, even as institutions kept buying gold miners (Newmont, SILJ) into Reddit's souring silver sentiment -- a contrarian setup worth watching, not a thesis break.

Market breadth did NOT confirm Monday's bounce: NYSE decliners (1,761) still beat advancers (945), and only 3 of 11 sectors have a majority above their 200-DMA -- this remains a narrow, mega-cap-driven rally.

Singapore banks (DBS/OCBC/UOB) extended a mark-to-market selloff after a Citi downgrade; OCBC reports Q3 on Nov 6 and CapitaLand China Trust reports Oct 23 after selling CapitaMall Yuhuating to shore up its balance sheet.

China's rare-earth export-control pause lapses Nov 10 with no extension yet published -- the single biggest near-term catalyst for the MP/Lynas/Energy Fuels watchlist; Lynas just committed ~A$968M to a Brazilian heavy-rare-earth project (Meteoric Resources) directly into that window.
Fed stays in blackout into the Oct 27-28 FOMC (hold odds ~84-87%, hike tail ~14-15%, cut effectively priced at zero) -- this is a hold-but-hawkish Fed, not a dovish pivot.

regime.label: Equities bounce, AI credit stays distressed: a fragile risk-on with live two-sided catalysts
regime.oneLiner: Monday's broad equity rebound (Nasdaq +1.11%, VIX -7.75%) is real, but Oracle and SpaceX setting fresh CDS records the same day shows credit markets are far less convinced than equities that the AI-financing scare has passed.

topNews.headline: Credit investors still won't believe the AI-debt rally has ended
topNews.actionable: Treat renewed CoreWeave/Oracle CDS widening as an early warning to keep the cash pile intact and avoid AI-capex-adjacent credit risk; it's also a tailwind for GDX/SILJ as a safe-haven hedge if contagion resumes.

topNews.headline: China's rare-earth export pause nears Nov 10 expiry with no extension yet published
topNews.actionable: The unresolved Nov 10 deadline is the single biggest near-term catalyst for the MP/Lynas/Energy Fuels watchlist -- continued Beijing silence into early November should be read as bullish for Western rare-earth supply-chain names.

topNews.headline: China Q3 GDP beats at 4.5%, but investment and retail sales stay weak
topNews.actionable: The export-led beat is modestly supportive for Tencent/Xiaomi/SMIC and China-exposed SGX names, but soft retail sales and falling investment argue against chasing the China-consumption leg of the book.

topNews.headline: Singapore banks hit by mark-to-market losses after Citi downgrade sparks selloff
topNews.actionable: Avoid adding to SG bank exposure ahead of the Nov 6 OCBC print; reassess bank weighting only after Q3 results clarify whether the losses are earnings-relevant or technical.

topNews.headline: Silver/SLV whipsaws as institutions buy SILJ dip while Reddit sentiment turns bearish
topNews.actionable: The split between institutional accumulation and souring retail sentiment is a classic contrarian setup -- don't get shaken out of SILJ/SLVP/GDX positions on short-term technical breaks.

signals: No call cleared the strong-signal bar (pUp3m ≥0.6/≤0.4 with confidence ≥0.55) this run -- today's set is more balanced-to-cautious than conviction-driven; the closest are SLV (pUp3m 0.60, confidence 0.45) and GLD (pUp3m 0.58, confidence 0.48), both Overweight on the commodities stance.
Watch the silver/gold-miner complex (GDX/SILJ/SLVP): institutions (Newmont, SILJ buyers) are accumulating into a Reddit sentiment downturn on SLV -- a contrarian setup rather than a thesis change.

Watch the rare-earth basket: Lynas's ~A$968M Meteoric Resources deal is a genuine re-rating catalyst (LYC.AX pUp3m 0.58) directly ahead of China's Nov 10 export-pause deadline, while MP Materials carries a fresh insider-selling caution flag despite a similar pUp3m (0.54).

Consider the AI-credit divergence (HYG pUp3m 0.46, confidence 0.37; LQD pUp3m 0.49): CoreWeave eased from distressed levels but Oracle/SpaceX set fresh CDS records the same day -- credit, not equity, is the cleaner read on whether AI-financing stress is really over.

Watch XLF (pUp3m 0.59, confidence 0.50, the highest-confidence call this run): a likely Fed hold plus strong Q3 bank earnings momentum supports financials even as the AI-credit story keeps equities two-sided.
